A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SorryDB study. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures and Lean examples are readable, allowing reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 1,000 SorryDB tasks, including prover accuracy, sampling curves, tactic analyses and qualitative proof examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluation and adds inference-cost results, estimated prover Elo ratings and a task-difficulty distribution.

M1.justification: The repository extraction, filtering, deduplication, LeanInteract verification and prover procedures remain unchanged. Expanded task explanations and proposed governance policies do not establish changes to the implemented proving or extraction methods.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,000-task sample from 5,663 tasks across 78 repositories and five categories. Table 4 retains identical repository membership and task counts, including Verina despite removal of its accompanying discussion.

E2.justification: The corresponding performance tables evaluate the same tactics, general-purpose models, specialized provers, self-correcting configurations and agentic configuration. The newly cited Requena et al. work is not introduced as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix K adds supplementary Elo scoring from per-task comparison outcomes. The existing sample-selection procedure, deterministic tactic evaluation, pass@1/pass@32 evaluation and 16-iteration budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an evaluation-cost comparison and an Elo-based analysis of task difficulty in Appendices I and K. The Brownian-motion and CLT examples, tactic study and prover-complementarity analyses already existed in v1; their relocation does not constitute new experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix K newly describes statistical estimation through a Bradley-Terry fit, jointly estimating task and prover ratings on a logistic scale. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-seed uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Kimina's main-table pass@1/pass@32 changes from 1.0%/6.6% in v1 Table 1 to 1.8%/7.7% in v2 Table 2, with its sampling curve also revised. Other main-table scores remain unchanged. Tables 5 and 6 and Figure 13 add cost, Elo and difficulty results. However, Table 6 lists Kimina at 6.6% and Gemini Pro at 20.6%, conflicting with Table 2's 7.7% and 20.5%; no different settings are explained.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements and Lean proof examples are retained. The new Elo section invokes an existing statistical model without adding formal mathematical definitions, theorems, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a dynamic benchmark reflecting real Lean work, automated validation, complementary provers and the effectiveness of iterative feedback. Additional appendix analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly distinguishes tool access's aggregate benefit from occasional retrieval over-reliance. The limitations now emphasize that the agent is a simple baseline, while Appendix J acknowledges potential contamination and the imperfect novelty signal provided by goal-state hashing.

D1.justification: v2 adds README-based evaluation/submission guidance, permanent repository-category labeling details, and governance policies for immutable YYMM snapshots, six-month releases and contamination audits. v1 only suggested periodic, potentially monthly updates. Table 5 adds token totals and estimated costs, identifying self-hosted estimates as upper bounds.

R1.justification: v2 adds Requena et al. (2026) as agent-design context and Bradley and Terry (1952) for rating estimation, while removing the Ye et al. (2025) Verina discussion and reference. The broader positioning against competition benchmarks and existing project-based evaluations remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology edits, expands explanations of task granularity and categories, adds results subheadings, and moves the qualitative analysis from Appendix A into Section 4.2. An impact statement and new appendix sections are added, but most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v1 Figure 3 is split into separate figures; the qualitative proof figure and dataset-composition table move into the main text. v2 also adds cost and Elo tables and a difficulty-distribution figure.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves practical transparency through inference-cost reporting, explicit snapshot and contamination policies, and clearer qualifications about tool use and the baseline agent. These gains are limited by the sparsely specified Elo estimation and conflicting accuracies in Tables 2 and 6. The central evaluation and conclusions remain largely unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
